input: working on tools for a christian babysitting sole prop single operator business. taxes. scheduling. lead gen lead qualification. reference request/elicitation storage and management. marketing website, automated sales. automated marketing. content marketing. this is an ongoing project for a friend. / other potential features that would be helpful. / i don't think browser only is required / lets have 10 agents work on this project.
errors: First preflight failed: count files (sync_tree_counts, sync_readme_counts) were stale after adding a venture; regenerated and committed.
Nine lane posts had descriptions over 160 characters; shortened before merging.

doc_friction.issue: regen --verify reported that a generator wrote outside gitops/prod/ and named my new post and ledger file, but git status was clean afterwards; the message reads like data loss when it was only the count checks that needed fixing.

deviations.why: The user asked for 10 agents mid-run, so the foundation PR also seeds 10 parallel lanes, each on its own claude/babysit-<lane> branch and PR, instead of one branch per session.
deviations.did: Landed the foundation first, then dispatched 10 worktree agents with separate module files and small additive edits to shared files.

deviations.why: The brief names its own work (a friend's babysitting business), so it takes precedence over the default of deepening the top flagship.

notes: 43 tests pass (run_venture_tests.py babysitting-business-kit). clauses.mjs 2/2 pages pass, validate.py passes, launched.json updated. Playwright smoke at 390px: every tab, add lead, add sit with live quote, tax panel, settings persisted across reload, no page errors (the only console line is the sandboxed website-preview iframe refusing inline script, which is intended). Tax constants come from sibling ventures that checked them against IRS/SSA. Ten lane agents (worktrees) each opened a PR (#11598, #11599, #11601, #11603, #11604, #11612, #11613, #11614, #11615, #11617). I merged all ten branches into this PR's branch with merge commits so their PRs close as merged when this one lands, resolving shared-file conflicts: a union for the Dockerfile COPY and server FILES lines, both-sides for additive blocks, and by hand where lanes collided: slots.mjs and site.mjs were both imported as S (site renamed SITE); the desk PUT ran keepIntakes before mergeReferences (a stale app copy undid a referee's answer, caught by references.test.mjs); the ?ref= prefill moved from the old buildSite into site.mjs; /site/blog had to precede /site/; self-host.html lacked 15 variables other lanes added (deploy.test caught one; the test now scans all server modules). 197 tests pass, including the Playwright e2e; my own Playwright pass at 390 and 1280 px over all 11 tabs had no page errors.

pricing.source: Anthropic pricing as cached in the Claude API skill (models table and per-model migration notes), 2026-10-06. Cache writes are 1.25x input (5-minute) and 2x input (1-hour); cache reads differ by model.

human_equivalent.basis: a developer building a 1,000-line app, 300-line server, tests and a guide page from scratch

certainty.tokens: high: summed from the per-request `usage` the API returned, as the transcript recorded it, deduplicated by message id
certainty.model: high: the `model` field on each API response, not the configured model
certainty.api_equivalent_usd: medium: measured tokens x list prices in prompts/pricing.json (as_of stated); an equivalent, not a charge: these runs are billed under a subscription
certainty.time: medium: from transcript timestamps; model time is request-to-response, tool time is call-to-result, time waiting on a person is excluded from active time
certainty.human_equivalent: low: the agent's own estimate of how long a competent person would take, with its basis written down; never measured

not_counted: requests the harness makes outside the transcript (context compaction summaries, title generation, safety classifiers), if any
transcripts lost when a cloud session moved to a new container: only files present in this container are read, so a resumed session can undercount
server-tool fees (web search is billed per search, not per token); the count is recorded, not priced
CI minutes and the reviewer bots' own model calls
